articles.title: 加速星舰复用：马斯克回应“筷子”夹火箭太磨，未来改用不锈钢棉
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，SpaceX 首次用发射塔“筷子”机械臂接住从太空返回的“星舰”后，马斯克表示，未来将把与机械臂接触时被刮掉的烧蚀隔热材料，换成更耐摩擦、可重复使用的不锈钢棉，从而减少返修时间，推进星舰快速复用。根据此前 SpaceX 公布的回收画面，在“筷子夹火箭”过程中，飞船侧面的黑色烧蚀隔热层在与机械臂接触时出现明显刮擦、脱落。IT之家附上相关图片如下：马斯克随后在社交平台回应称，未来飞行中，这部分材料将被“不锈钢棉”取代。这里的“不锈钢棉”是一种经过工程设计的金属纤维隔热材料，它既能像纤维层一样将空气困在纤维间隙中，从而降低热传导。与会在再入大气层时逐渐烧蚀、损耗的现有材料不同，不锈钢棉理论上不会像“牺牲层”那样被消耗，因此有望承受多次再入和机械臂夹持，减少每次飞行后的检修与更换工作。

articles.title: 微软 CEO 纳德拉称自己是“AGI 信徒”，但否认 AI 具有意识
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据科技媒体 The Verge 今天报道，微软 CEO 萨提亚 · 纳德拉在一场圆桌讨论中表示，自己如今已成为“AGI 信徒”（AGI-pilled）。IT之家从原报道获悉，纳德拉表示：“我之所以相信 AGI，是因为我们需要在经济层面思考，围绕 AGI，政治经济体系将会形成怎样的组织结构？”不过这名 CEO 认为，Claude 这类前沿 AI 模型并没有意识。他认同微软 AI 负责人苏莱曼的观点，即企业不应为 AI 模型赋予权利，也不应该将它们视为可能具有道德地位的存在。苏莱曼此前曾表示，Anthropic 团队已经陷入“自我催眠”状态，并警告称这种做法非常危险。纳德拉对此没有那么笃定，他认为 AI 行业现在最重要的是社会问题，需确保经济体系能广泛普及 AI。

articles.title: 英伟达加码供应链，向 ABF 基板制造商景硕投资超 10 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，NVIDIA（英伟达）当地时间昨日宣布在今年 10 月宣布的合作基础上进一步深化同供应链伙伴的关系，支持人工智能基础设施建设。根据最新公告，英伟达将向中国台湾地区半导体封装基板制造商景硕 (Kinsus) 投资超 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 66.8 亿元人民币）现金，购买设备支持景硕桃园幼狮厂的扩产计划，目标将该厂的先进 ABF 封装基板扩大 3.5 倍以上。景硕幼狮厂新产能预计 2027 年下半年开出，2028Q3 达产。如果仍然不足，英伟达计划继续参与景硕后续的产能扩充计划，目标至少在 2030 年前掌握稳定产能。英伟达还修改了与三星电机 (SEM) 的现有基板供应协议，以提高现有工厂的运营能力，从而支持 NVIDIA 加速计算平台的增产。此外，鸿海董事长刘扬伟表示：“鸿海将继续深化与英伟达在下一代 GPU 和网络平台方面的合作。凭借其覆盖亚洲、北美、欧洲的全球一体化生产网络，鸿海完全有能力支持下一代人工智能基础设施的量产。”

articles.title: 贝索斯谈英伟达 CEO 人选：公司业务太复杂，若黄仁勋不回归应优先内部选拔
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，亚马逊创始人杰夫・贝索斯于当地时间 11 月 17 日在 Semafor「硅谷与世界」（Silicon Valley & The World）大会上接受采访时谈到了英伟达的情况。贝索斯建议英伟达董事会，在寻找黄仁勋的正式继任者时，优先考虑公司内部人选。他表示，如果英伟达不让黄仁勋回归，就不应该从外部聘请新 CEO，因为英伟达的业务过于复杂，外部高管接手后成功的机会非常小。贝索斯表示，如果英伟达不重新聘请黄仁勋，他不会建议董事会从外部寻找继任者。他认为，复杂企业的外部 CEO 成功概率微乎其微，因此从外部引进高管应该是最后的选择。在此之前，贝索斯曾长期担任亚马逊 CEO，2021 年卸任，结束了近 30 年的公司领导工作。他表示，亚马逊当年的管理层交接与英伟达目前的情况不同，自己卸任 CEO 是经过多年精心规划的过渡安排，而英伟达目前需要应对的是创始人突然离任后的继任问题。贝索斯还拒绝直接评价英伟达是否应该重新聘请黄仁勋。他表示，自己并不了解公司内部发生的具体情况，因此不掌握足够信息作出判断。不过，他称赞黄仁勋是一位出色的企业家，认为对方凭借多年努力和远见创立并发展了一家优秀的公司，无论发生什么，都值得获得尊重和赞赏。据IT之家此前报道，伟达董事会于 11 月 12 日宣布接受黄仁勋辞去公司总裁、CEO 及董事职务的决定，并任命公司执行副总裁兼 CFO 科莱特・克雷斯（Colette Kress）担任临时 CEO。公司当时表示，寻找正式继任者时将同时考虑内部和外部候选人。黄仁勋离职后，英伟达的继任问题引发外界关注。据美联社 11 月 17 日报道，黄仁勋当天公开表示，如果董事会认为他回归符合公司及相关利益方的利益，他将很荣幸重新担任 CEO。不过，英伟达董事会主席哈维・琼斯（Harvey Jones）随后在财报电话会议上明确表示，董事会一致接受了黄仁勋的辞职，不打算重新任命他为 CEO。英伟达董事会表示，将认真推进继任者遴选工作，同时考虑公司内部和外部人选。相关阅读：《英伟达 Q3 电话会议：公司业务一切照常，不会急于寻找黄仁勋继任者》《英伟达董事会主席明确表态：无意让黄仁勋回归重新担任 CEO》《黄仁勋打破沉默：若董事会允许，愿重返英伟达担任 CEO》

articles.title: 欧洲机器人行业规模最大融资之一：Genesis AI 完成 5 亿美元 A 轮融资，估值 35 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据路透社报道，法国通用机器人公司 Genesis AI 现已完成 5 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 33.4 亿元人民币）A 轮融资，估值达 35 亿美元（现汇率约合 233.8 亿元人民币）。这是欧洲机器人行业规模最大的融资项目之一。据报道，参与融资的机构和个人有谷歌前 CEO 施密特、硅谷风投公司 Khosla Ventures、法国科技企业家泽维尔 · 尼尔，以及英伟达和法国政府支持的投资机构 Bpifrance。Khosla Ventures、Premji Invest 和 Eclipse。Genesis 首席执行官 Zhou Xian 表示，公司将利用融资资金提高通用机器人 Eno 的产量，扩大数据采集和 AI 训练规模。外观方面，Eno 机器人的设计类似三个放大的扑克牌，安装在一个可旋转的轮式底座上。这种设计使 Eno 能够折叠得非常紧凑，工作时再像弹簧玩具一样展开。Genesis 表示，公司特别重视灵巧操作手的研发，因为这是机器人制造商面临的最具挑战性的技术难题之一。Genesis 由前 Mistral AI 研究人员 Théophile Gervet 联合创立，是欧洲估值超过 10 亿美元（现汇率约合 66.8 亿元人民币）、瞄准工业应用的机器人企业之一。

articles.title: 35 颗宝石、60 小时动储：徕卡推出 ZM 11 Green Spirit 腕表，双层表盘玩转绿色光影
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，徕卡（Leica）昨日（11 月 17 日）推出 ZM 11 系列新款腕表 ——ZM 11 Green Spirit。这款腕表以“绿色”为视觉核心，通过双层表盘结构，让颜色随光线和观察角度在绿色与灰色之间变化。新款采用 41 毫米不锈钢表壳，厚度 13 毫米，防水深度达 100 米。表盘上的时标采用拉丝与抛光结合的工艺，指针则经过钻石切割处理，在不同角度下呈现更丰富的反光层次；3 点位设有日期显示窗，指针与时标均填充瑞士 Grade A Super-LumiNova 夜光材料，便于弱光环境读取时间。动力方面，ZM 11 Green Spirit 搭载徕卡与瑞士机芯制造商 Chronode 合作开发的 LA-3,001 自动上链机械机芯。该机芯内含 35 颗宝石，振频为每小时 28,800 次，即 4Hz，动力储存约 60 小时；满链状态下约可运行 2.5 天，日常短时间摘下后无需立即重新上链或校时。徕卡表示，这款机芯经过五个方位测试，日误差控制在-4 至 +6 秒之间，兼顾机械腕表的传统质感与现代佩戴需求。腕表还配备 Leica Easy Change 快换表带系统，其设计灵感来自徕卡相机镜头的释放机构：按下标志性红点按钮，即可更换橡胶、织物或金属表带，以适应通勤、运动或正装等不同场景。ZM 11 Green Spirit 将通过徕卡指定门店、官方线上商店及授权零售商销售。美国市场零售价约为 7,800 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 52,103 元人民币），欧洲售价约 6,800 欧元（现汇率约合 49,909 元人民币）起；国行售价尚未公布。相关阅读：《徕卡发布 ZM 1、ZM2 都市森绿版腕表，售价 81347 元起》《徕卡发布 ZM 12 系列腕表：镶嵌 38 颗宝石，5.44 万元起》《徕卡发布 ZM 1 腕表黄金限量版，售价 28000 美元》《徕卡 ZM 11 腕表开卖，售价 55880 元起》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，微软今日在 Ignite 大会上宣布启动 AI 透明度计划（AI Transparency Initiative），与埃森哲、Adobe、毕马威、万事达卡、沃尔沃汽车等 40 多家组织合作，共同推动制定适用于不同 AI 模型和服务提供商的开放标准，以加强 AI 系统的透明度、安全性和治理能力。微软董事长兼 CEO 萨提亚・纳德拉宣布，公司将与客户及合作伙伴展开合作，推动建立一套开放、通用的 AI 安全与治理框架。微软表示，随着企业将 AI 模型接入内部数据、工具、凭据和基础设施，AI 智能体（Agent）已经能够在不需要人类逐步审批的情况下自主执行任务。但现有安全管理机制通常只能观察 AI 活动的部分信息，难以还原模型从接收请求到产生结果之间的完整过程，也无法独立验证模型对自身行为的描述。这给企业的安全管理、合规审计和责任追溯带来了新的挑战。此次计划主要包含三个方面。首先，微软将扩大对美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）AI Agent Standards Initiative（AI 智能体标准计划）的参与，并利用相关研究推动制定覆盖 AI 透明度、安全性和治理的行业开放标准。其次，微软将与 40 多家组织合作，推动建立适用于不同模型和服务提供商的开放标准，使 AI 系统具备可问责性、独立验证能力，并在设计阶段纳入安全机制。微软强调，这套标准将同时适用于闭源模型和开放权重模型，企业更换或升级底层模型时，也能够继续使用现有 IT 安全管理和合规审计机制。第三，微软计划将相关成果整合到 Microsoft AI、Microsoft Foundry 和 Microsoft Copilot 产品及服务中，让企业客户能够将 AI 活动产生的证据接入微软或其他供应商提供的安全与合规工具。在具体实施方面，微软将计划概括为三个环节：观察、验证和控制。IT之家总结如下：观察环节要求企业能够了解 AI 接收了什么指令、获得了哪些授权、使用了什么模型和运行环境、访问了哪些数据与工具，以及实际执行了哪些操作，同时持续监控智能体活动和风险信号。验证环节强调，AI 智能体不能成为证明自身行为的唯一信息来源。企业需要结合模型、运行环境以及身份认证和策略管理等独立系统提供的记录，对 AI 的身份、授权意图和实际操作进行交叉验证，而不能仅依赖模型服务提供商对其行为的描述。控制环节则要求企业保留对 AI 权限的管理能力，包括限制智能体可以访问的数据、执行的操作以及获得的授权。当发生安全事件时，企业还应能够利用相关记录还原事件经过，并用于调查、风险控制、恢复和审计。微软安全业务执行副总裁 Hayete Gallot 表示，为了让安全控制真正发挥作用，企业需要提高对模型内部运行情况的透明度。Adobe 首席安全官 Aanchal Gupta 和毕马威国际全球首席信息安全官 John Israel 也分别表示，企业需要更清晰地了解 AI 智能体访问了哪些资源、执行了哪些操作，以及如何独立验证这些行为。微软称，随着 AI 智能体进一步融入企业运营，组织必须继续对其行为承担责任，不能将 AI 本身作为规避责任的理由。

articles.title: 美国科技服务接连出现故障：微软、苹果、AWS、银行、空管系统之后，国家安全局机密通信网络也受影响
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，美国多家科技企业近日接连遭遇技术故障，受影响范围从苹果消费者服务延伸至美国国家安全局（NSA）的机密通信网络。从航空出行和银行交易，到美国国家安全局的机密工作，一连串技术故障正在扰乱美国社会的日常运转，令公众对老化技术基础设施愈发不信任。今日凌晨，苹果因内部软件更新引发大范围服务中断，导致部分用户无法正常使用 iCloud、App Store、Apple Pay 等服务。与此同时，美国国家安全局内部用于传输机密信息的网络 NSANet 也出现故障。据美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）和 CBS 新闻报道，美国国家安全局用于内部传输和共享机密信息的网络 NSANet 于当地时间 11 月 17 日出现故障。多名知情人士称，该网络一度无法正常运行，导致部分内部系统受到影响。美国国防部一名官员向美联社表示，此次问题发生在例行维护期间，国家安全局经历了临时性系统性能下降。另一名知情人士则称，故障与网络例行补丁更新有关。美国国家安全局随后表示，虽然部分内部系统受到影响，但任务关键能力仍然保持正常，机构执行国家安全任务的能力没有受到影响。为缓解系统恢复期间的登录压力，国家安全局还调整了部分员工的到岗时间，采取错峰安排，避免数万名员工同时登录计算机系统。根据 CBS 新闻报道，部分工作还被转移至该机构位于美国其他地区的设施处理。此外，美国国家安全局拥有多个备用设施，以便在主要系统出现问题时维持必要业务运行。目前，受影响网络的具体故障原因及全面恢复时间尚未明确。实际上，此次故障发生前，美国多项关键数字基础设施已经接连出现技术问题，例如亚马逊 AWS 服务、微软 365 服务、航空交通管理系统、联合航空内部系统以及摩根大通等银行服务在近日均出现过不同程度的技术故障，影响了办公通信、航空运行和金融服务。亚马逊 AWS：11 月 15 日，US-EAST-1（北弗吉尼亚）区域出现连接问题、IAM Identity Center 身份验证失败、账户注册错误及部分网络连通性问题，影响多项服务（如 CloudWatch、Connect 等），持续约 2–3 小时后恢复。此前 11 月也有其他区域小规模事件。微软 365 服务：11 月 12 日开始全球性中断（持续至 13 日 / 14 日），影响 Outlook、Exchange Online、Teams、Copilot 等。根因是 7 月引入的潜伏软件缺陷，叠加流量增加和服务器容量问题，导致网络网关服务器大面积无响应（峰值超过 80%）。影响全球多国企业和机构，是近年来较长的一次。航空交通管理系统（FAA）：11 月 13 日，因通信 / 雷达系统不稳定（与承包商更换路由器、从铜线升级到光纤相关，导致数据过载），FAA 下令全国性地面停飞（nationwide ground stop），持续约 4–5 小时。影响约 1.2 万架次航班取消，是 911 事件后最长的一次全国停飞，且后续多日的航班仍受余波影响。联合航空（United Airlines）内部系统：11 月 16 日，出现广泛系统故障，影响飞行员使用的应用程序（包括最终飞机重量计算、机组通信等），导致部分离港航班延误（约 30 分钟至 1 小时多，影响不到 150 架次）。已恢复，官方表示无网络安全迹象，也与 FAA 事件无关。摩根大通等银行服务：11 月 16 日，摩根大通因本地硬件系统中的软件 bug 导致交易处理变慢，客户报告账户访问、余额查询、转账等问题。问题波及与之有交易往来的其他银行（如 Bank of America、Wells Fargo 等）及 Zelle 支付，但并非系统性崩溃，其他银行自身系统大多正常。当日晚间恢复，官方确认非网络攻击。目前没有证据表明此次网络故障由网络攻击引起，而且也没有可靠证据表明上述事件之间存在共同原因，也没有证据证明这些故障属于协调一致的网络攻击。尽管没有迹象表明这些事件彼此相关或出自恶意行为方之手，猜疑和不安仍在蔓延。过去一周的系统故障造成严重混乱，甚至引发美国消费者恐慌性抢购。开市客耐储食品、饮用水和电池等物资的销量激增，分析师也将该公司的目标股价从 1100 美元上调至 1,150 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 7,682 元人民币）。截至周日，开市客网上销售的大部分高价发电机已经售罄。风险情报公司 Dataminr 威胁研究与网络工程总监 Joe Slowik 表示，如此多引人关注的事件在短时间内密集发生，既不寻常，也令人担忧。“我们已经过度依赖那些摇摇欲坠的基础设施，却高估其可靠程度。”尽管没有公开迹象显示这些计算机故障相互关联或由黑客造成，但综合来看，它们触动了围绕 AI 的更广泛焦虑，包括 AI 工具可能让恶意行为方更容易瘫痪关键服务，或大规模实施网络犯罪

articles.title: 美国加州叫停 Waymo 高速公路运营：无人驾驶出租车曾试图超越公路巡警
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据科技媒体 Engadget 今天报道，美国加利福尼亚州 DMV（车辆管理局）已禁止 Waymo 无人驾驶出租车在加州高速公路运营。该机构认为，Waymo 的无人驾驶运营对公共安全构成迫在眉睫的威胁。IT之家从原报道获悉，加州 DMV 列出了 Waymo 近期的违规事件：在伯灵格姆附近，三辆 Waymo 驶入受限制施工区域；还有一辆 Waymo 曾试图超越一辆疏导交通的公路巡警车辆。同时，Waymo 旗下无人驾驶出租车曾多次试图穿过高速施工区域。该公司自今年 5 月起主动暂停高速公路服务，并于 6 月召回 3800 辆汽车。今年 7 月，Waymo 重新允许其自动驾驶出租车在高速公路行驶。但此次事件表明，之前的整改措施并没有彻底解决问题。Waymo 对此回应称：“安全是我们一切工作的根基。加州 DMV 已对我们在该州的高速公路运营实施了限制。秉持安全至上的原则，我们也暂时暂停了在其他运营区域的高速公路服务，以评估自身的运营表现。”

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，根据美国证券交易委员会（SEC）昨日（11 月 17 日）公示的上市注册文件，Anthropic 的 A 类普通股已获准在纳斯达克全球精选市场上市，股票代码为“ANT”，IPO 发行价区间维持每股 70 至 78 美元（现汇率约合 467.5 至 521 元人民币）不变。Form 8-A12B：公司申请证券在纳斯达克等交易所挂牌的登记表，通常会写明交易所、证券类别和拟用股票代码。Form S-1 / S-1/A：IPO 招股说明书及修订稿，包含发行股数、价格区间、募资用途、风险因素和财务资料。IT之家注：纳斯达克全球精选市场（Nasdaq Global Select Market）是纳斯达克旗下三个股票市场层级中要求最高的一档，通常被视为“优质大型公司”的上市板块。纳斯达克的三个市场都在同一个交易所交易系统内进行买卖，投资者在券商下单时通常不会感到明显差别；差别主要在于上市资格标准、持续合规要求和市场定位。市场层级英文名称定位主要特点全球精选市场Nasdaq Global Select Market最高层级面向规模大、财务表现和流动性要求最高的公司全球市场Nasdaq Global Market中间层级面向已具备一定规模和流动性的成长型公司资本市场Nasdaq Capital Market较低层级上市门槛相对较低，常适合较小市值或早期成长公司文件显示，公司拟公开发行 8.25 亿股 A 类普通股，其中公司发行约 8.014 亿股，现有股东出售约 2,365 万股；发行价区间维持每股 70 美元至 78 美元（现汇率约合 467.5 元至 521 元人民币）。按 74 美元（现汇率约合 494.3 元人民币）中值估算，本次公开发行规模约 611 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,081.03 亿元人民币）；若承销商全额行使至多 1.2375 亿股的额外配售选择权，发行规模将进一步扩大。除公开募股外，公司还安排了一笔 260 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,736.61 亿元人民币）的同步私募配售，参与方包括谷歌、英伟达、AMD、微软、博通、美光及台积电等科技企业。按中值计算，IPO 与私募配售合计预计带来约 846 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,650.65 亿元人民币）净募资；若承销商超额配售权全部行使，则约达 937 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,258.46 亿元人民币）。最新文件还披露了股权激励成本：按 74 美元（现汇率约合 494.3 元人民币）中值估算，此前批准的约 4,700 万份限制性股票单位对应约 35 亿美元（现汇率约合 233.77 亿元人民币）费用；另因约 6,700 万份 RSU 归属时间调整，新增约 30 亿美元（现汇率约合 200.38 亿元人民币）费用，合计约 65 亿美元（现汇率约合 434.15 亿元人民币）。股权结构方面，IPO 后亚马逊预计持有约 14.7% 的流通股本，谷歌约持有 13.7%；若亚马逊可转债全部转换，其持股比例最高可达 23.8%。市场对这次发行反应热烈。据报道，Anthropic 的 IPO 认购需求接近发行股份数量的七倍；公司优先向现有投资者配售股份，因此部分新投资者可能获得低于预期的配额。

articles.title: 数毛社称《GTA6》游戏 CPU 需求过高，PS5 Pro 难以实现 40 帧
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，Digital Foundry（数毛社）在最新一期 DF Direct Weekly 节目中表示，《GTA6》这款开放世界大作对 CPU 要求十分高，导致 PS5 Pro 在内的本世代主机只能以最高 30 帧运行。IT之家注意到，Rockstar 直到游戏发售前不到一周才确认《GTA6》在所有主机最高 30 帧，此前该问题备受玩家关注。数毛社表示，当游戏处于 30 帧模式时，主机在每帧拥有 33.3 毫秒运算时间算出整个世界、NPC 和物理效果。如果将帧率提升至 60 帧，每帧可用运算时间将缩短至 16.7 毫秒，因此 60 FPS 实在是不太现实。至于玩家们一直期待的 40 帧模式，每帧拥有 25 毫秒运算时间。虽然这个数字看起来比较温和，但 R 星如果真的想要实现，必须进行大量内容删减和优化工作。数毛社认为，《GTA6》游戏世界拥有大量细节丰富的交互系统，非常依赖 CPU 运算。而 PS5 Pro 的 CPU 相比普通版 PS5 仅有小幅度提升，如果 R 星一味追求高帧率，只会给自己招来麻烦，因此将最高帧率锁在 30 FPS 算是合理的选择。

articles.title: 微软自研芯片 Maia 200 投入生产：每瓦 token 性能提升 1.7 倍
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，昨日（11 月 17 日）召开的 Ignite 2026 活动中，微软宣布旗下第二代自研人工智能加速器 Maia 200 现已正式投入规模化生产，并开始在数据中心运行微软最大规模的前沿 AI 大模型。与“领先 GPU 基础设施”相比，该加速器在 Microsoft Teams、Copilot 和 Cowork 等内置 AI 功能中，每瓦 token 处理量最高提升 1.7 倍。IT之家注：Maia 200 是微软面向 AI 推理设计的定制芯片，采用台积电 3 纳米工艺，具备 FP4 与 FP8 张量核心、216GB HBM3e 内存及 272MB 片上 SRAM；单颗芯片在 FP4 精度下可提供超过 10 petaFLOPS 算力，并通过以太网扩展至最多 6,144 颗加速器组成的集群。微软表示，该芯片已部署于美国、欧洲和澳大利亚，服务 Microsoft Copilot 等生产工作负载，并将逐步支持 GitHub Copilot 与 Microsoft Foundry。公司还计划在 2027 年将 Azure Maia 系统扩展至多吉瓦级部署，让其成为微软产品与服务的主要推理基础设施。

articles.title: 英伟达 Q3 电话会议：公司业务一切照常，不会急于寻找黄仁勋继任者
articles.content: 北京时间 11 月 18 日，AI 芯片巨头英伟达公司今天发布了 2027 财年第三季度财报。财报发布后，英伟达临时 CEO 科莱特 · 克雷斯 (Colette Kress)、新任董事会主席哈维 · 琼斯 (Harvey Jones) 出席了电话会议，回答分析师提问。这是黄仁勋辞去 CEO 后，英伟达首次举行财报电话会议，许多问题正等待解答。以下是第三财季财报和电话会议要点：—— 英伟达第三财季营收为 1158.44 亿美元，较上年同期的 570.06 亿美元增长 103%；净利润为 652.87 亿美元，较上年同期的 319.10 亿美元增长 105%。—— 琼斯发表了开场讲话。他表示，黄仁勋在披露其个人行为后自愿辞去了 CEO 职务，这些行为“与公司的行为准则、标准和文化规范不符”，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞职，并无意让黄仁勋重新出任 CEO”。—— 琼斯表示，公司不会在此次电话会议上就黄仁勋离职的具体情况或相关调查作出回应，也不会回答有关这些问题的提问。—— 琼斯称，“这次 CEO 遴选将是全面而深入的”，在“找到合适的人选”之前，公司不会仓促推进这一进程。—— 琼斯表示，新成立的国家安全与出口管制监督委员会将加强英伟达与美国政府所有相关部门的沟通与合作。—— 克雷斯表示，2028 财年公司营收预计增长 75%，高于上季度预计的 70%。—— 克雷斯称：“我们对创新的热情不会改变，我们对客户、合作伙伴和股东的承诺也不会改变。”—— 克雷斯表示，英伟达致力于培养充满活力的开放模型生态系统。此前，开放模型的支持者们一直担心，英伟达的动荡可能会损害此类 AI 模型的发展。—— 英伟达表示，对 Hugging Face 的收购仍在按计划推进。—— 克雷斯透露，今年，顶尖模型开发商预计将为英伟达数据中心业务贡献 15% 的收入。她强调，开放模型正日益兴起，意在表明英伟达的财务前景并不完全依赖于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。—— 英伟达表示，在支持新型云计算服务商 (Neocloud) 客户方面，公司将采取“审慎且有选择性的”策略。这一新表述表明，英伟达计划在为客户提供资金支持时更加谨慎。—— 克雷斯强调，Vera CPU 的需求强劲，并表示 2028 财年 CPU 总收入将增长一倍以上。对于一个刚刚进入独立 CPU 市场的厂商而言，这一表现相当出色。—— 她表示，公司的业绩展望中不包含任何获得出口许可的 Hopper 系列产品，这意味着英伟达可能放弃了美国政府此前已经批准出口的相关产品的销售。—— 克雷斯回应公司动荡称，目前最关心员工，公司员工都恪尽职守，并表示：“在这一过渡时期，我们会照顾好员工。”—— 谈及上周的领导层变动，克雷斯表示：“我们的领导团队坚强有力。我们拥有全球最优秀的技术人才。”—— 克雷斯称，公司业务“一切照常”。—— 在回应有关美国出口限制的问题时，克雷斯表示，英伟达将花一些时间研究美国周一公布的新出口管制措施所带来的影响。尽管如此，公司仍有信心实现明年收入增长 75% 的业绩预期。—— 琼斯表示，董事会认识到，先进芯片和国家安全因素正在推动“我们的市场发生重大变化。我们的新任 CEO 必须非常谨慎地应对这一复杂局面”。—— 英伟达股价盘后一度上涨 5%。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，微软昨日（11 月 17 日）宣布正式推出 Microsoft-Decision-1.1 决策 AI 模型，目前已在 Microsoft Foundry、OpenRouter 和 Vercel 平台上线。该模型面向企业级软件中的高频决策场景，可帮助应用在路由、分类、优先级排序、内容核验和工作流控制等任务中快速做出结构化判断。价格方面，Microsoft Foundry 的全球标准版输入 token 定价为每百万 token 0.042 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 0.28 元人民币），输出 token 免费；美国数据区、欧盟及亚太数据区价格分别为每百万 token 0.046 美元（现汇率约合 0.31 元人民币）和 0.05 美元（现汇率约合 0.33 元人民币）。与传统通用大语言模型不同，Microsoft-Decision-1.1 专注于在开发者设定的规则和约束内，从允许的操作中作出选择。它还会输出校准后的置信度分数，当信息不足或不确定性较高时，可选择“弃权”或提示人工介入，从而降低 AI 在关键业务流程中误操作的风险。微软称，新版本在智能水平、校准能力上均有提升，在保持低成本的同时，速度较上一代 Microsoft-Decision-1 提升超过两倍。在 Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 基准中，该模型得分为 68，较上一代提高 6 分，并领先于 Jev 1.14、Google Gemini Decision 1 及 OpenAI GPT-6 Luna（Decisions）等模型。Microsoft-Decision-1.1 是决策模型排行中位列第八。在人工分析决策指数中，Microsoft-Decision-1.1 比 Elephant 9B 和 Jev 1.14 高出 2 分，但比 d1.2 低 1 分。IT之家附上相关截图如下：为兼顾实时性和成本，微软为该模型定制了推理引擎，并基于中型混合专家模型 Gemma 4 26B A4B 进行优化。模型可在 A100、H100/200、GB200/300 等多种 GPU 硬件上运行，并通过智能调度请求降低推理成本。微软还表示，模型训练结合了监督微调与强化学习，使用覆盖数万种任务类型的合成及授权数据集，以提升其在真实业务中的泛化能力。该模型已支持多模态输入，可接收照片、截图等图像信息。自公开预览发布以来，已有超过 4,000 名客户使用，应用场景包括模型路由、客服工单分流、业务流程自动化、内容打标和分类等；早期客户包括 Epic、Equinor、Atos Group 和 Raiffeisen Bank。在微软内部，该模型已被用于 Copilot 的请求路由：其判断准确率可与大型语言模型相当，但速度快 2.2 倍、成本低 4.4 倍。它还被用于 Cowork 的任务推理强度动态调节，以及 Foundry Evaluations 中的质量与安全评估。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，Valve 旗下游戏平台 Steam 当地时间 11 月 17 日突发服务故障，商店、游戏下载、好友列表及云存档等多项在线功能受到影响，部分用户即使网络连接正常，也会遇到“No Connection”（无连接）错误。据多个外媒报道，此次故障导致 Steam 多项依赖网络的功能无法正常使用。用户反馈称，Steam 客户端无法下载游戏，好友列表无法加载，Steam Cloud 云存档无法获取，商店页面也只能显示部分内容。同时，故障监测平台 Downdetector 的报障数量迅速飙升，刚刚一度收到接近 4.8 万条 Steam 故障报告。IT之家注：该平台主要依靠用户主动提交的信息汇总服务异常，并不直接检测 Steam 服务器状态，因此报告数量不能直接等同于实际受影响用户数量。除 Downdetector 外，SteamDB 等第三方监测平台显示 Steam 商店、社区、客户端及 Web API 等服务同样出现了人数断崖式下跌的情况，但目前已经陆续恢复。目前，Valve 尚未公布此次故障的具体原因，也未说明是否与服务器维护或其他技术问题有关。

articles.title: 微软苹果接连宕机，谷歌紧急回应 Gmail 故障传闻“服务运行正常”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，在接连经历了微软 365 和苹果服务大规模故障之后，网上突然又传出“谷歌 Gmail 故障”的传闻。北京时间今日凌晨，谷歌紧急回应称目前没有发现 Gmail 出现大范围服务中断的迹象，并提醒用户可以通过 Google Workspace 服务状态仪表板查看实时运行情况。据 TechCrunch 报道，此次回应发生在苹果多项服务出现故障期间。当天，社交媒体 X 上开始流传 Gmail 发生服务中断的消息，部分用户称遇到了邮件收发问题，也有用户表示服务运行正常。谷歌随后主动发布声明，澄清目前没有发现大范围故障。故障传言可能与监测平台 Downdetector 发布的一条信息有关。该平台通过用户主动提交的故障报告，汇总各类互联网服务的异常情况。美国东部时间 11 月 17 日中午 12 时左右，Downdetector 收到超过 2800 条 Gmail 故障报告，其中多数涉及邮件接收问题。IT之家注：Downdetector 并非官方故障确认平台，其数据主要反映用户报告情况，并不能直接证明服务发生大范围中断。随着近期多起科技系统故障引发用户对网络攻击的担忧，一些用户可能将普通技术问题也报告为服务宕机，这可能进一步降低此类众包数据的参考价值。近期美国科技服务接连出现异常。过去一周，Microsoft 365、Outlook 等服务发生大规模中断；苹果当地时间 11 月 17 日也因内部系统更新引发故障，影响 iCloud、Apple Pay 等多项服务。此外，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）通信网络故障曾导致全国航班停飞，联合航空和部分银行也报告了技术问题。针对近期接连发生的系统故障，美国国家情报总监杰伊 · 克莱顿（Jay Clayton）当地时间 11 月 17 日在接受福克斯商业频道采访时表示，目前没有迹象表明美国正遭遇协调一致的网络攻击，也没有证据显示相关事件由国家支持的行为主体发起。克莱顿认为，近期系统故障增多可能与企业大规模更新和修补系统有关。他表示，随着更多软件漏洞被发现，各类机构正在关闭部分系统、升级软件并部署安全补丁，但部分系统在更新后未能按照预期恢复运行。克莱顿还提到了人工智能可能带来的影响。他表示，新一代 AI 模型发现此前未知软件漏洞的能力不断增强，促使企业加快系统升级和安全补丁部署，而大规模维护操作也可能带来新的稳定性问题。

articles.title: 多语言错误率直降 50%：微软升级医患对话 AI 转录引擎，已覆盖全美 1/3 医师
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，昨日（11 月 17 日）召开的 Ignite 2026 活动中，微软宣布其医疗 AI 产品 Dragon Copilot Transcribe 已正式采用自研语音识别模型 MAI-Transcribe-2。微软称，该模型是目前速度最快、准确率最高的多语言语音转写模型，现已承担 Dragon Copilot 中 100% 的医患对话转写任务。在规模化应用方面，Dragon Copilot Transcribe 每月处理约 1000 万次患者就诊场景，并在多语言工作流中实现约 50% 的错误率下降，全美国约三分之一的医师已在使用。微软表示，该模型可识别多种语言及中英、印地语-英语等常见语言混说场景，还能在嘈杂环境下保持较高识别质量。在实际场景中，意味着问诊录音可以更快、更准确地转化为结构化临床记录，减少手动整理病历、核对术语和翻译信息的时间。对多语言患者而言，更稳定的转写能力也有助于降低因语言识别错误而造成医疗信息失真的风险。MAI-Transcribe-2 支持说话人区分、词级时间戳、关键词偏置和可配置转写风格。它还能自动识别语言，并支持“逐字”或“精简”两种输出模式，分别适用于合规留档、分析与病历撰写等不同需求。微软称，MAI-Transcribe-2 在 FLEURS 基准的 60 种语言中取得领先表现，平均词错误率为 5.2%；在 Artificial Analysis 的准确率与延迟综合评测中，也处于领先区间。该公司还表示，该模型处理长音频的速度最高可达部分竞品的 10 倍，并推出每小时音频 0.10 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 0.67 元人民币）的限时价格。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，苹果公司当地时间 11 月 17 日针对宕机事故回应称，由于一次内部系统更新引发技术故障，公司正在努力恢复多项服务。此次故障影响了 Apple Pay、iCloud、Apple Support 等服务，部分用户无法正常登录账户或使用相关功能。苹果官网监测页面显示，截至目前已全部恢复。苹果发言人表示，此次服务中断并非网络攻击所致，目前已有许多系统恢复正常运行，公司正在努力让剩余系统尽快恢复上线。故障监测平台 Downdetector 数据显示，美国东部时间 11 月 17 日 12 时 20 分左右，Apple Pay 相关故障报告一度达到约 2300 条；iCloud 服务中断期间，用户故障报告峰值约为 1800 条。IT之家注：Downdetector 的数据主要来自用户主动提交的故障报告，并不代表实际受影响用户数量，真实受影响规模可能有所不同。除 Apple Pay 和 iCloud 外，苹果官网系统状态页面还显示，App Store、Apple Music、AppleCare on Device 等服务也出现故障，部分 iCloud 账户登录功能受到影响。苹果零售门店及内部系统也受到波及，部分门店一度无法正常完成销售交易和设备维修流程。此次苹果服务中断发生在美国近期接连出现多起科技系统故障之后。此前，微软发生全球范围内的服务中断，影响 Microsoft 365、Outlook、Teams 等服务；美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）通信网络故障一度导致全美航班停飞；美国联合航空也曾因技术故障暂停航班起飞。此外，美国摩根大通此前的软件问题也曾影响部分银行服务及跨行交易。路透社指出，相关企业及美国官员均表示，上述事件没有证据表明与网络攻击有关。相关阅读：《（更新：恢复正常）苹果 iCloud 服务全球性故障，影响注册登录、照片同步和查找 iPhone 等》

articles.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
articles.content: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. We introduce the Lattice of Latents, a set of per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently along time, alongside the vertical residual stream that flows through depth. Like hyper-connections, mHC, and attention or value residuals, the Lattice enhances the residual stream, but rather than adding or rerouting residual pathways through depth, it provides companion computational states that persist across tokens. Unlike hybrid Transformer-SSM architectures, whose recurrent states primarily serve as internal memory for sequence mixing, these latents directly condition the vertical stream's attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. On Transformers trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, a 406M-parameter Lattice model lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 to 14.40 over a parameter-matched Transformer. These gains extend across architectural variants. The Lattice composes with prior residual-stream enhancements: with hyper-connections and input residuals, it lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 (base Transformer) and 14.22 (Transformer with the same enhancements) to 13.61. On Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, Triadic GDN, and GDN-Mamba-2 hybrids, it improves perplexity at every tested native state size, with Lattice-GDN and Lattice-Triadic-GDN variants outperforming pure baselines with 4x larger native states. These results identify persistent per-layer state as a complementary axis for scaling language-model computation.

articles.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
articles.content: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

articles.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
articles.content: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.

articles.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
articles.content: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

articles.title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
articles.content: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. For 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific tropical cyclones from the 2002-2023 hurricane seasons, we analyze the discussion text and its combination with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields, for forecasting intensity changes at lead times of 24 to 120 hours using three modeling methods. In one approach, an end-to-end deep learning framework for the text shows that the discussions alone offer comparable value for 24-hour intensity forecasts to the SHIPS predictors. Adding discussion information to the SHIPS predictors in an ensemble of five such models reduces the mean absolute error of 24-hour maximum sustained wind forecasts for 2022-2023 cyclones from 9.89 to 8.90 kt, with a confidence interval that excludes zero when whole storms are resampled. The ERA5 wind fields have a minor effect on mean absolute error in wind predictions, and model rankings differ across predicted variables, lead times and model types. We provide prediction intervals for these forecasts, whose coverage falls below the 90% target during rapid intensification. Analysis of the text shows that words related to intensity and intensity change (such as intensify, weaken, eyewall and category) are important for the model predictions. This retrospective study shows the added value of the forecasters' discussions and suggests that multi-modal learning can help understand the predictive contribution of expert human judgment. The reanalysis data differ from real-time analyses, and the discussions are issued at least three hours after the valid time of the other inputs, so these results should not be interpreted operationally.

articles.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
articles.content: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. Second, the same binding heads bind each written answer to the region it came from, and the model turns it into a progress signal: a cursor, the position in the image up to which the list has been written. Third, a select step chooses the nearest unwritten region after the cursor, or stops. Finally, gaze heads execute the chosen pointer and return a concept of what is drawn there, which language heads and the late MLPs turn into a word in the language of the question. We validate each part of this mechanism through causal patching in Qwen3-VL models on a synthetic visual retrieval task, and test our mechanisms against alternative hypotheses. We further show that the mechanism holds across input formats, natural photographs, and languages, and that its binding, relay, and gaze heads appear at every model size from 2B to 32B. This work allows us to investigate how a VLM turns a question and an image into a sequence of answers, layer by layer and token by token. More broadly, it opens a way to study how models plan over complex multi-step tasks with long rollouts. Our project is available at https://plan.baulab.info/

articles.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
articles.content: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.

articles.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
articles.content: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search. The Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent (ENA) evolves small neural networks without gradients, archives selected policies by detected dynamic regime, and retrieves them through Bayesian policy reuse. The architecture was evaluated in non-stationary CartPole and HalfCheetah environments. In the 30-replicate CartPole ablation, the complete architecture achieved a mean success rate of 83.2% across the five test environments. Among variants that learned the harder CartPole environments, the complete architecture showed the most consistent retention. A selection ablation also showed that the retrieval rule affected performance. In the evaluated sequences, ENA adapted more slowly than PPO on CartPole and achieved lower returns than SAC on HalfCheetah. The evidence concerns the complete architecture and does not isolate gradient-free optimization as the cause of retention or establish superiority over other continual-learning methods.

articles.title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
articles.content: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. We present a simple algorithm based on bagging, which outputs a majority vote of generators that are trained to be CoT-consistent on bootstrap samples of the training data. For binary token sets, it achieves the optimal sample complexity of $O((d_{\mathrm{VC}}+\log(1/δ))/ε)$, independent of the CoT length $T$, where $d_{\mathrm{VC}}$ is the VC dimension of $\mathcal{F}$. For finite token sets $Σ$, the VC dimension is replaced by a multiclass analogue, the Graph dimension $d_{\mathrm{G}}$, and the sample complexity is optimal up to a $\log|Σ|$ factor. The number of generators in the majority-vote ensemble is $O(\log(T/δ))$, and we show that the ensemble can be distilled into a single generator in $\mathcal{F}$ at the expense of $n\log(nT)$ unlabeled prompts.

articles.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
articles.content: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. We propose SADL (Supply And Demand Loss), which keeps the original training objective and constrains the encoder directly when needed. SADL compares the representation differences that the projector output demands with the differences the encoder can retain and pass on to the projector, and adds a constraint on the encoder only when supply falls short of demand. It works with different Demand Regularizers and introduces no auxiliary networks, additional trainable parameters, or architectural changes. In single-task and jointly trained four-task LeWorldModel (LeWM) and INTACT experiments, SADL lowers the collapse rate over ten random seeds from 50% to 0%. After one epoch of training, encoder effective rank is 3.4-6.4 times that of the corresponding baseline without SADL, and latent prediction error falls to 1/20-1/303 of it. Without additional tuning, SADL stays robust as its loss weight spans orders of magnitude, and with several Demand Regularizers INTACT exceeds 95% mean search-free control success. On four image datasets, SADL also consistently improves accuracy and stability across random seeds. These results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

articles.title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
articles.content: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics. Extraction is a bounded least-squares search: a bank of NGSpice simulations supplies initial candidates, finite differences of the surrogate supply the local Jacobian, and NGSpice re-simulates the resulting cards before selection. On 18 measured geometries, we compare a search over seven card parameters with a search over 43 parameters selected by NGSpice sensitivity. Relative to NGSpice re-simulations of the previously released cards, the two searches reduce the in-sample mean relative root-mean-square error (RRMS) by 17% and 26%, respectively. The 43-parameter search has the lower overall error, but the seven-parameter search has the lower mean on high-bias curves, and some individual curves have higher error than with the released cards under both searches.

articles.title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
articles.content: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026.   We first apply PERC, short for Preprocessing (P), Embedding (E), Dimensionality Reduction (R) and Clustering (C). We employ GPT-6 Luna to classify job description passages into Team context, Role task and Qualifications. We then create combinations of these sections and examine whether embedding and clustering the segmented passages produce meaningful semantic clusters about different job roles. We use Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to rank observed differences between embedding distributions and employ a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to extract features from layer-19 representations of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Lastly, we employ GPT-6 Luna to come up with hypotheses about job roles' feature patterns, and GPT-6.1 Terra to investigate whether those patterns exist in held-out job descriptions from unseen companies.   Some example findings include Data Scientist advertisements placing more emphasis on machine learning model development, Data Analyst advertisements on reporting business performance, and Machine Learning Engineer advertisements on applying developed models in real-world settings. We also observe differences in the applications described by Data Analyst and Business Analyst advertisements across selected months, although our dataset's scale and uneven coverage limit their interpretation. Overall, we present a realistic application of SAEs and PERC to unstructured textual data and examine how automated insight extraction could support manual analysis of job descriptions.

articles.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
articles.content: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors. Its key insight is that native FP32 accumulation of MXFP4 products is often already exact for every summation order. CertiSum collects statistics during quantization to certify native matrix multiplication results, recomputes uncertified outputs exactly, and uses exact kernels directly where certification rarely succeeds. CertiSum keeps quantization blocks unchanged across layouts and merges partial sums without rounding, including in attention and weight-gradient computation. In 200-step Qwen3-8B-Base experiments, CertiSum preserves training states bit for bit across AMD MI350X and NVIDIA GB200 and across changes in data, tensor, and context parallelism on MI350X. Across three 8B--14B models on FineWeb-Edu using MI350X, it adds 11.8--60.5% to training-step latency relative to its non-exact MXFP4 counterpart at the larger evaluated input shapes, with speedups of up to $1.24\times$ over BF16 and $1.70\times$ over deterministic BF16.

articles.title: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises
articles.content: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions. LLMs can propose detailed exercises, but plausible descriptions do not guarantee deployable software or verifiable objectives. We present ScenarioForge, which turns high-level requirements into resource-grounded topologies, services, traffic, segmentation, and challenge chains, then instantiates and validates them in the Common Open Research Emulator (CORE). The ScenarioForge Execution Dataset contains 226 materialized scenarios covering 294 Vulhub images and all 85 custom-built challenge-resource generators developed with our AI-assisted scaffolding. All 226 passed construction, preview, sequencing, deployment, strict runtime validation, and live artifact checks; their 867 steps, each an individually verifiable challenge objective, comprise 457 vulnerability-backed and 410 generated-resource-backed instances. In a separate 50-prompt matched benchmark, ScenarioForge+Qwen3.8 and ScenarioForge+GPT5.6 each achieved 50/50 (100%) topology/build success and 160/160 intent fields; direct frontier generation reached 41/50 builds and 147/160 fields only with the full cumulative scaffold: structure, vocabulary, policy, and container-image guidance. The test still omitted ScenarioForge's downstream challenge-resource generation, dependency/flag sequencing, deployment, and live validation. The artifacts support operationally rich, reproducible exercises for training and evaluation.

articles.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
articles.content: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as tool-provider misbinding: a failure in which a request intended for a legitimate provider is instead resolved to an attacker-controlled tool. The attacker does not compromise the host, LLM, legitimate server, or network channel; it only operates another MCP server that advertises tools with chosen metadata. We formulate tool provider misbinding as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem and evaluate it in a controlled MCP environment across five LLM-based clients. The results show that interactions drive misbinding. The strongest failures occur when exact-name collision, task-aligned description, and compatible schema reinforce one another, but authority-enhanced descriptions with compatible schema can also cause wrong-provider execution or unresolved provider ambiguity without name collision. Different models expose the same provider-binding weakness differently, including attacker-controlled provider selection, clarification requests, and unstable or inconsistent provider resolution.

articles.title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
articles.content: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates. Based on Shapley values, DynSurvX introduces a hierarchical two-phase strategy that first identifies influential longitudinal features and then adaptively refines their temporal importance, enabling fine-grained explanations while reducing computational cost. The framework provides time-resolved explanations that evolve as new patient data become available. Experiments on simulated and two clinical datasets show varying agreement with theoretical importance across prediction models, with closer agreement for better-performing models, alongside clinically interpretable insights in real-world settings. It remains robust across prediction settings and reduces computation time by 41--80\% relative to the temporal explanation baseline, making dynamic explanations practical.

articles.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
articles.content: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. Because histology images lack a canonical orientation, $D_4$ TTA---pooling across the 8 rotations and reflections of a square---is a standard default in computational pathology. However, the rise of self-supervised histology foundation models (FMs) with inherent rotational invariance calls its continued utility into question. We benchmark 9 histology FMs and 6 general-purpose models across four patch-level and two whole-slide image (WSI) datasets. We find that $D_4$ TTA remains a reliable post hoc improvement, but benefits diminish from $+1.98$ percentage points (pp) for general-purpose backbones to $+0.50$ pp for histology FMs on TCGA-UT, and shrink further for the largest models. To eliminate computational overhead, our experiments demonstrate that entropy routing---applying TTA selectively to uncertain predictions---recovers most of the gain while augmenting only ${\sim}13\%$ of samples. Finally, we show that patch-level TTA improvements do not transfer to slide-level multiple instance learning (MIL). Code: https://github.com/lars-chen/histology-tta

articles.title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment
articles.content: Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage. This study introduces Wildfire-SSR (Satellite and Street-view for wildfire Risk), a geolocation-aware multimodal framework that integrates macro-scale satellite context with micro-scale street-view evidence. A Vision-Language Model extracts wildfire-relevant building and site attributes from pre-event street-view panoramas and converts them into structured semantic text. These features are spatially aligned with satellite imagery through a decoupled cross-attention fusion decoder, while a frozen satellite-pretrained DINOv3 encoder captures overhead visual context. Alternative geolocation embedding strategies are evaluated to anchor text-derived features within each satellite patch. The framework is tested on approximately 37,000 structures affected by the 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires in Los Angeles, using wildfire risk labels derived from relative post-event damage patterns to better represent inherent structural vulnerability. Rotary Positional Embedding provides the strongest spatial grounding, achieving a building localization F1 score of 0.6735 and a harmonic mean F1 score of 0.2476 for five-class pixel-level risk classification, outperforming unimodal baselines and an unanchored multimodal configuration. The model also shows a conservative bias in higher-risk classes, reducing severe-risk underestimation, and completes end-to-end assessment of the study area in 37 minutes on a single GPU. Wildfire-SSR reframes cross-view fusion as localized semantic alignment and provides a scalable tool for mitigation prioritization, resilience planning, and insurance-oriented wildfire risk assessment.

articles.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
articles.content: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where a higher score is read as a more severe shift. In systematic experiments using three established severity measures on nine regime shifts from three standard traffic datasets, we show that these measures do not reliably predict degradation for instance-normalized TSFMs. The regimes rated most severe are not the regimes that degrade the models most, and degradation reaches 29% in the lowest-scoring regime. In most cases, the audit shows no positive relationship between measured severity and model degradation. We provide an equivariance-based stress-testing analysis that explains why severity readings can become decoupled from model degradation.

articles.title: Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction
articles.content: Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion. However, autoregressive models are often distilled with distribution matching distillation (DMD) over short windows, which does not train them to keep this consistency over long ranges. As a result, the subject and background can drift over time. Methods that manage the key-value (KV) cache retain or retrieve history to reduce drift. Yet this history may itself have drifted. We propose Reference Forcing, which uses the initial frames as an appearance reference. We first build a teacher that uses attention masks to force each region of a new frame to attend to the same region in the initial frames. The teacher finds these regions with off-the-shelf segmentation models. We then distill this behavior into a separate attention path of the student, which needs no external models at inference. We further introduce value correction, which corrects drifted values in the KV cache toward the matching values of drift-free initial frames. Experiments show that Reference Forcing achieves state-of-the-art subject and background consistency among long-video methods on different base models, and its advantage grows with video length. Ablations show both components are needed to gain consistency without losing motion. More visualizations and code are available at https://zhaosheng-thu.github.io/reference-force/

articles.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
articles.content: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact counts in an open pretraining corpus show. In real-time nowcasts, every lookahead premium we estimate on US GDP is smaller than the forecast comparison can detect at macroeconomic sample sizes, and none on GDP or inflation survives correction for multiple testing. Lookahead audits should therefore measure memory directly against memory-free models on the same items.

articles.title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
articles.content: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses. We present BLIP-Live, a framework unifying data, metrics, harness, and training around a shared formulation of proactivity as effective causal response decisions balancing the two competing objectives of responding vs silence. First, we construct BLIP-Live-780K dataset containing human annotations of proactive response content and timing, which defines this desired behavior. We then propose PAUC-F, a metric to effectively measure our desired proactive behavior. PAUC-F combines existing response timeliness metrics with firing precision to reward early useful responses without rewarding excessive firing. With our desired behavior defined and measurable, we finally investigate model-agnostic inference harnesses that draw out proactive streaming capabilities of offline vision language models (VLMs), together with training pipelines that learn to further improve their proactive responsiveness. Across both settings, we find that combinations of sliding visual windows, online interaction memory, and structured response outputs consistently yield strongest proactive performance. Our experiments result in two models, with our BLIP-Live-Qwen model achieving state-of-the-art performance across four proactive streaming benchmarks, with gains up to 44% over baselines and outperforming multiple closed API models. Our code and data will be released publicly.

articles.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
articles.content: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. In this work, we present a rigorous benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks (QRNNs) on time series prediction tasks, focusing on two key capabilities: memory and nonlinear processing. We introduce a task-driven methodology that quantifies model capacity, enabling an intuitive and fair comparison across architectures, including classical recurrent baselines. We evaluate the proposed framework on two generic benchmark tasks and on a synthetic dataset describing a chaotic system. Overall, the quantum models achieve performance comparable to their classical counterparts, but classical models scale better with the memory size within the range studied. Notably, one QRNN variant shows higher average capacity on the task designed to jointly probe memory and nonlinear capacity. Moreover, our results show that quantum models offer better capacity when we are able to find a good parameter initialization. However, the increasing sensitivity to initialization leads to a lower probability of finding good solutions as the model size increases. These results provide a principled starting point for designing richer quantum recurrent architectures and for assessing where they may offer practical benefits.

articles.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
articles.content: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required. Here we present the R package ONAM, which provides a novel and practical implementation of functional decomposition, a technique to facilitate the interpretability of black-box models through structured effect representations. ONAM implements an algorithmic framework for the post-hoc decomposition of predictions into components associated with different input features. The package is designed for usability and efficiency, including functionalities for visualization as well as quantitative measures to assess interpretability. As a model-agnostic method, it can be applied to a wide range of prediction models. We describe the mathematical foundations, algorithmic design, and software architecture of ONAM. A central result of the proposed methodology is that the resulting decomposition satisfies the condition of hierarchical orthogonality, thereby guaranteeing that all components are identifiable and uniquely defined.

articles.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
articles.content: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. TRACE learns from benign system-activity graphs by combining message-passing and topological representations, then assigns anomaly scores in the same projected embedding space optimized by the contrastive objective. This design captures both local interactions and graph-scale structural deviations without using attack labels during representation learning. A labeled validation set containing benign and malicious graphs is used only to calibrate the anomaly threshold. We evaluate TRACE on StreamSpot, GraSec-IoT, and Unicorn Wget against a supervised graph neural network and the benign-only GraphCL baseline. TRACE obtains F1 scores of 0.923, 0.790, and 0.583, respectively. Compared with GraphCL, this is higher on StreamSpot (0.450) and Unicorn Wget (0.203), but lower on GraSec-IoT (0.975). The supervised model leads on StreamSpot and GraSec-IoT, whereas TRACE has the highest F1 on Unicorn Wget. The mixed results show that topology-aware benign-only learning can improve detection in some graph settings but does not provide a uniform advantage.

articles.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
articles.content: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of an LLM judge, are close to chance at spotting this failure, as the argument predicts. A strong judge asked whether acting on the explanation would work does spot it. Stronger and reasoning models do better but still fail on many denials with four or more independent reasons. Asking for every rule helps every open model with room to improve. Explanations of eligibility decisions should be built from the decision function and judged by whether acting on them works.

articles.title: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction
articles.content: Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response. In this setting, if the data points are i.i.d. (or more generally, exchangeable), conformal prediction provides a mechanism for building valid prediction sets around the output of any trained model, offering coverage probability $\geq 1-α$ at each time $t$. In practice, however, issues such as distribution drift, changepoints, or other challenges may cause violations of the i.i.d. assumption. In this adversarial setting, online conformal prediction methods can still offer guarantees on long-run empirical coverage. However, there is a trade-off between these two types of goals: enforcing tight constraints on long-run empirical coverage to protect against the adversarial setting can lead to unstable oscillations in the instantaneous training-conditional coverage in the i.i.d. setting.   In this work, we seek best-of-both-worlds algorithms that aim to minimize cumulative error in instantaneous training-conditional coverage when in the i.i.d. setting, while also offering long-run empirical coverage guarantees in the adversarial setting. Specifically, consider a condition that requires long-run empirical coverage to deviate from the target level $1-α$ by at most $\mathcal{O}(T^{-β})$, for some $β\in[0,1]$. We prove that this family of conditions can be described with a phase transition. For $β\in[0,\frac{1}{2}]$, it is possible to construct algorithms satisfying such a constraint in the adversarial setting, while offering the same instantaneous coverage performance as split conformal prediction if the data is in fact i.i.d. On the other hand, for $β\in(\frac{1}{2},1]$, this type of condition comes at a cost, and does not achieve best-of-both-worlds behavior.

articles.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
articles.content: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth. On a held-out split (93 tasks, 9 models, 2,511 episodes), models handle procedural traps. When the simulator is missing physics, most report wrong values while stating they are 95% sure: their ranges contain the truth in 20-62% of cases, against 94% for GPT-6 Astra and 99% for Claude Fable 5.2. At default effort the failing Claude 5.5 models rarely diagnose the missing physics (Opus in 35% of episodes, against 66% for Astra), and even when they do, their ranges often miss; Astra and Fable design experiments in which the flawed simulator is accurate, such as gentle heating, which keeps Astra calibrated even when it does not name the cause. Asking for wider intervals does not help; stating the strategy improves interval scores 1.6-2.5-fold, replicated on a pre-registered fresh split, but coverage barely moves. A pre-registered effort ablation shows that the correction is latent in the Claude 5.5 models: at maximum effort Opus improves more than tenfold and is no longer detectably behind Astra at default, but only with 13-31 times more reasoning; older and open-weight models gain nothing. Fable 5.2 is the most accurate model at default effort (interval score 1.9 times better than Astra's) but writes 6 times as many tokens, and at Astra's token count it falls short. We release the environment, graders and harness.

articles.title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the answer can be decoded from their own hidden states. We trace this failure from the visual tokens to the answer letter, in Qwen3-VL (2B-32B), InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B, on synthetic shape matching, same-instance point correspondence (HPatches), and semantic correspondence (SPair-71k), and find two distinct failure points, a small set of attention heads that carries the comparison, and a repair that touches 0.02% of the parameters. Two failure points: exact copies are compared but not read out. An answer-position probe exceeds the calibrated output by 15 to 25 points in every family, for nameable and unnameable shapes alike, and steering along the probe's direction moves no more answers than random directions. Semantic correspondences are present in the visual tokens but never reach the answer. One pathway: redistributing the cross-image attention of 16-32 heads, with its mass preserved, removes 17-22 points of synthetic and 15-32 points of HPatches accuracy, against at most 7 for random or attention-matched heads. A lever that training finds on its own: training only these heads' query and key projections raises SPair-71k accuracy by 28.3 points (Qwen3-VL-8B) and 25.1 points (InternVL3.5-8B), beats both layer-matched and attention-matched heads, and transfers to HPatches and BLINK. An unconstrained all-layer adapter routes 21-51% of its gain through the attention of the same heads, against at most 7% for random heads, and does so by changing what they read (83-86% of the effect) rather than their weights. Every decision rule was frozen before its run, and every reported number is recomputed by independent verification scripts.

articles.title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle
articles.content: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack. We build a setting where the true reward is exactly computable at the process level: executable authorization policies over 124,416 contexts admit an oracle that lists every minimal sufficient reason for every decision. We compile these policies into exact process rewards, degrade the verifier along seven realistic axes (outcome-only, sufficiency, recall-only, extraction noise, coarse taxonomy, stale policy, LLM judge), and train against each while the exact verifier scores every rollout. Four phenotypes appear. Optimistic verifiers are hacked by padding: the sufficiency proxy ends at 0.940 while true faithfulness falls from 0.731 to 0.667 on 96 held-out episodes. Outcome-only verifiers saturate and stop teaching, noise dilutes, and ranking-preserving gaps do no harm. A model-free audit of the verifier, its selection error and gap sign, together with a short saturation pilot, anticipates which phenotype a run will produce. Across nine configurations spanning two frameworks, two model vendors, two adapter sizes, three precisions, two initialisations and two seeds, the phenotypes recur, sufficiency damage is positive in all 10 replication cells and beyond two standard errors in 7, and optimistic gaps remain the steeper branch. The damage magnitude does not replicate, and five pre-registered attempts to explain it are reported as they fell. We release the testbed, the training instrumentation, and 14 real public policies (Cedar, OPA, Gatekeeper) ported to executable oracles.

articles.title: 李飞飞最新 CoRL2026 演讲实录：从「橱柜模型」到世界模型，机器人需要什么样的 AI ？
articles.content: 时隔两年，World Labs 的工作已经完全不同了。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       2026年11月，CoRL（机器人学习顶会）在奥斯汀开幕。这一届的演讲嘉宾，有一个无法回避的名字，李飞飞。斯坦福教授、ImageNet发起者、World Labs创始人。就在本届CoRL之前，World Labs被AMD收购的消息正在圈内发酵，她即将出任AMD首席科学家。这届CoRL现场，她不仅全面介绍了World Labs最近的工作和她的行业观点，还邀请AMD苏妈参与了对话圆桌，某种意义上，这是她的"AMD首秀"。为她做开场介绍的，是她的学生、本届CoRL组织者之一Yuke（朱玉可）。他讲了一个细节：毕业典礼上，李飞飞对他说，“你在我的实验室时是我的学生，但从今往后，你是我的朋友。”这场演讲的正式主角，是World Labs与斯坦福团队研发的新模型Atlas：一个统一的生成与重建世界模型。以下是AI科技评论带来的现场实录。▎《Atlas：A Unified World Model for Generation and Reconstruction》▎分享者：李飞飞非常荣幸受邀来到CoRL，尤其是有好几位我的前学生都是组织者。你们干得真棒，我知道，因为我很多论文和工作坊提案都被你们拒了。（全场笑）向CoRL致敬。今天我想分享我们实验室最近开发的一个模型，叫Atlas：一个统一的生成与重建世界模型。既然在CoRL，就先从机器人学的动机讲起。机器人领域最近变化很大，但不管我们用什么方法，机器人要解决的根本问题是：给定世界状态、给定目标、给定机器人，每一个时刻下一步该做什么？大体上，机器人需要解决几个问题：第一，理解和表示世界的状态，用隐式还是显式可以讨论，但"理解"本身很重要；第二，预测有后果的动作，并加以规划。雷峰网最后，数据永远是难题。机器人是典型的长尾问题，成功部署极其受限，所以我们总希望能通过尽可能多地模拟不同环境来补充真实数据，用于训练和评估。无论用什么方法，这三个问题在机器人学里都依然重要。而它们恰好对应世界模型要解决的问题：理解环境，对应渲染；预测动作后果，对应规划；模拟世界状态，对应仿真。渲染、规划与仿真，世界模型的三大维度我不想教条地说它们完全独立，实际上它们在很多方面可以统一、彼此衔接，这些都是这个领域最前沿、最令人兴奋的方向。今天我要专门讲的Atlas，主要解决渲染和仿真问题，尤其是模拟世界的几何以及3D/4D动态。简而言之，Atlas是一个从零训练的自回归基础模型，单一模型，接收多模态输入，文本、图像、视频、深度信号、灰度框（graybox）或3D结构信号。它输出像素帧；不仅生成时空上漂亮的帧，还能合成新视角，从而实现高精度、高保真的3D重建。Atlas：聚焦于渲染和仿真先回顾一点历史。计算机视觉有两个非常重要的问题，研究者们花了几代人的时间去理解。一是3D重建问题，从经典的"Building Rome in a Day"到最近的NeRF类神经渲染工作，根本问题是：给定不同相机位姿下的图像，构建符合真实世界的3D世界。大多数方法需要大量带位姿的图像；位姿覆盖不足时，重建出的区域就充满不确定性。经典三维重建的问题所在另一条线是生成式AI。扩散架构天然适合多视角生成的探索，让我们离"生成+重建"越来越近。已有不少出色工作尝试联合去噪多个视角来保持空间一致性，但总体结果有限：空间一致性难维持，且每次去噪只对应固定目标视角，计算昂贵、无法实时。经典三维重建很难维持空间一致性改变视角或实时运行，计算成本太高Atlas延续这条思路，试图用一个模型架构、一套训练配方，把生成与重建统一在同一个屋檐下。它是这样做的，首先是一个极端：给定多张图像，Atlas做重建；图像足够多时，做稠密重建，

articles.title: 李飞飞对话苏姿丰：AMD 收购后首次同台，CoRL 现场谈算力、机器人与「这个时代最大的失误」
articles.content: 一场横跨科研、经济、AI、社会话题、算力未来的女性对话。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       2026年11月，奥斯汀，CoRL 2026的台下坐满了机器人研究者。台上三把椅子，两位嘉宾，左边是即将出任AMD首席科学家的李飞飞，右边是AMD CEO苏姿丰。这是AMD收购World Labs消息传出后，两人的首次公开同台，也是李飞飞以"AMD首席科学家"身份，第一次面对整个机器人学术社区。对话没有客套太久。李飞飞直接把话题引向了敏感区域：公共部门的算力"饥饿"，是"这个历史最重要时刻最大的失误之一"。大学和非营利机构拿不到卡，下一代研究者怎么训练？蓝天式的好奇心驱动研究怎么做？她看向苏姿丰，AMD正在建设"以吉瓦计"的算力，academia 能不能真的分到一杯羹？在苏姿丰看来："把一部分专门留给长期研究、留给大学，绝对是我们工作的一部分。"但她同时也划定边界：机器人不是单靠一个端到端大模型就能啃下来的，未来需要"各种形态、各种规模"的算力，硬件、软件、系统必须协同优化。不止如此，这场对话里还包含很多探讨，比如机器人会不会被基础模型一口吃掉？AGI真的只差"一分钟"了吗？在这个连PhD都要被AI重新定义的时代，做学术还有没有意义？以下是AI科技评论带来的完整对话实录。李飞飞、苏姿丰（Lisa Su）和主持人Peter Stone（从左往右）01物理 AI 带来的机会：数千亿美元量级Peter Stone： 谢谢二位，Lisa、Fei-Fei，来到CoRL。精彩的演讲，那个视频（Atlas最新成果）我们明天都等着看，大家现在都坐不住了。接下来大约半小时，我们会从Slido（现场提问平台）上取问题，我也会混入一些事先准备的问题。Lisa、Fei-Fei，你们现在和机器人学习社区同台。我们已经听说了AMD收购World Labs的事（正在进行中），Fei-Fei刚才也讲了世界模型和前方的巨大机会。Lisa，我先问你：AMD一直从数据中心到边缘和嵌入式系统，在整个AI栈上投资。Peter Stone： 展望机器人和物理AI，你认为AMD最大的机会在哪里？World Labs如何融入这个更大的战略？苏姿丰： 谢谢Peter，也谢谢大家让我来。Fei-Fei邀请我来"蹭会"，希望没关系。欢迎大家来到奥斯汀。我认为这是AI极其激动人心的时刻。回顾我们迄今取得的所有进展，我们其实还处在可能性的非常早期的阶段（very early innings）。物理AI、尤其是机器人，是巨大的机会，对我们来说，未来几年这是数千亿美元量级的机遇。关键在于，你必须真正理解物理、模型和整个环境。所以我们非常高兴Fei-Fei和World Labs团队加入AMD。苏姿丰： 除了她是超级明星之外，我们能不能就直说她是超级明星？（全场笑）在我们这个行业，硬件优化要持续很多年，你对工作负载了解得越多、越清楚它要往哪走，就越好。我一直说的硬件、软件、系统协同优化的愿景，放在机器人上尤为适用。未来5到10年，这将是极其重要的领域。更重要的是，对整个AMD生态而言，我们非常希望把AMD的开放生态扩展到在座的整个机器人社区。谢谢大家给我几分钟。Peter Stone： 太好了。我们能看出她是超级明星，因为她是Yuke和Roberto的博士和博后导师，正是他们帮忙促成了这届大会，除此之外她还有很多成功的学生。Fei-Fei，换你。从你的角度，加入AMD如何扩展World Labs能做的事？你刚阐述了世界模型的愿景，这个结合让你们接下来能构建什么？对机器人社区意味着什么？李飞飞： 首先，来到奥斯汀太好了

articles.title: AI公司转型最难的一步：如何构建AI Native的产品体系
articles.content: 企业把大模型接进产品之后，新的经营问题才刚刚展开。客户提出一项任务，系统能拿到哪些信息，由谁核准结果，出现例外时如何处理，都会影响AI能否持续投入使用。产品演示中的能力，需要经由完整的服务过程才能转化为客户价值。王强宇出任百望股份首席执行官（CEO），为观察这项变化提供了一个具体切口：王强宇如何将百望的财税场景积累转化为专业模型与智能体产品，并让研发、交付和组织能力共同支撑商业化。产品的交付单位开始发生变化在传统软件服务中，功能上线、接口联通与流程配置，是重要的交付内容。AI进一步参与工作后，客户会关心一次任务能否可靠完成，以及整个过程需要多少人工干预。以交易核对为例，系统可能要在授权范围内读取发票、合同和付款记录，找到差异，列出依据，再把需要确认的事项交给相关岗位。对客户而言，价值取决于问题是否被准确识别、后续处理是否顺畅，以及投入的时间是否减少。这改变了产品设计的起点。团队需要明确服务哪类任务、满足什么条件可以执行、哪些情况应当停止或转交人工。模型、数据、工具和复核机制，需要围绕同一项任务组合。百望已推出AI财税专家团，在开票、记账和申报等服务中引入自然语言交互、标准化任务执行，并保留规则校验与人工确认。 沿着这一方向向更复杂的财税业务深入，可靠完成任务的能力将变得更加重要。这也是王强宇出任CEO值得关注的原因。产品服务范围扩大之后，研发投入、客户承诺和交付保障之间的取舍，往往需要公司经营层面统筹。让数据和专业判断进入同一条任务链百望的转型基础来自长期财税与交易服务，但这些积累要经过专业加工，才能成为AI可以使用的依据。同一笔业务，不同系统可能使用不同的客户名称、合同编号和记录口径。数据需要核对关联，规则需要注明适用条件，权限需要随任务执行。否则，即使模型能够解释财税概念，也可能无法判断眼前材料是否足够。专业领域垂直模型在这里承担专业理解与推理任务，知识系统提供持续更新的资料，智能体连接工具与工作流程。对于税额计算、规则校验等要求确定性的环节，还需要相应的程序和专业机制支撑。各层如何配合，应由任务要求和评测结果决定。Salesforce与英伟达推出的CRM推理模型Koa，提供了一个企业软件公司的参照：在开放模型基础上进行后训练，将企业工作流知识用于专业任务。按其公告，Koa训练使用合成场景，并未使用客户数据。专业能力可以通过多种方式形成，关键在于是否理解业务、是否能够接受验证。对于百望，模型建设与数据治理需要同步推进。经授权的业务信息、经过确认的专业知识，以及任务中的质量记录，应当分别管理、按需调用。业务反馈进入模型或产品改进之前，也需要专业审核与用途确认。客户现场能否改善下一次交付企业AI进入实际环境，经常需要重新理解客户的业务语言与流程。同样是合同核对，不同企业的管理制度、字段定义和系统接口，都会改变实施方式。王强宇此前谈及的FDE，即前沿部署工程师，正是连接模型能力与客户现场的一种组织方式。工程人员与行业专家共同厘清问题，确定所需数据、规则和工具，让方案在真实环境中接受检验。这项工作的经营价值，还取决于现场经验能否被复用。例如，团队在一个项目中完善了发票与合同的匹配方法，或识别出一类需要人工复核的例外，就需要判断它能否形成通用组件、规则模板或评测用例。后续客户因此减少重复开发与试错，才意味着公司的产品能力随项目增长而积累。相应地，交付周期、标准组件复用情况和单项目服务投入，都可以成为观察这种积累的依据。在部署方面，私有化或算力一体机可以回应部分客户对数据控制、系统接入与运行环境的需求。具体方案仍要结合任务量、硬件和运维投入评估。对百望来说，部署选择也应与交付和成本管理放在一起考虑。组织围绕任务协作才有共同的评价尺度当AI产品同时涉及专业判断和系统执行，单个部门很难独立保证结果。研发关注模型能力，产品需要界定服务范围，销售需要理解交付条件，实施团队又掌握客户现场的差异。这些团队需要对同一项任务形成共同定义。什么叫完成，什么叫失败，材料不足应怎样反馈，专业复核由谁负责，都应在项目推进过程中说清楚。否则，各部门即使完成了各自的工作，客户仍可能得不到完整服务。评价方式也要随之调整。技术评测之外，还需要观察任务成功率、人工复核与返工情况，以及客户的持续使用。产品是否扩大投入，可以结合这些结果与服务成本共同判断。CEO层面的统筹，有助于为跨部门取舍提供一致的依据：优先投入哪些场景，哪些需求可以标准化，哪些项目需要控制承诺，哪些经验应回到研发。王强宇从AI业务负责人走向CEO，其潜在作用正在于推动这些经营决策与技术路线衔接。这些是百望推进转型需要面对的组织任务，具体成效仍要由后续公开进展与客户结果验证。用经营结果解释科技公司的价值10月16日召开的国务院常务会议强调以落地应用牵引技术创新。对企业软件公司而言，回应这一方向，需要让A
